Date of notice: 2026-08-20
Appeal deadline: 2027-02-16
Requested service: Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
Treating surgeon: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 (lumbar laminotomy/hemilaminectomy with decompression of nerve root) described in the above-referenced Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-20. The stated reason for denial is that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity."

**1. Identification of the governing policy**

Based on my review, the plan's applicable coverage document for this procedure is the UnitedHealthcare Oxford Clinical Policy titled "Spinal Fusion and Decompression." That policy states, in its Coverage Rationale section:

"Spinal procedures for the treatment of spine pain are proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances. For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP: Procedures: Decompression +/- Fusion, Cervical; Decompression +/- Fusion, Lumbar; Decompression +/- Fusion, Thoracic; Fusion, Cervical Spine; Fusion, Lumbar Spine; Fusion, Thoracic Spine; Scoliosis or Kyphosis Surgery; Scoliosis or Kyphosis Surgery (Pediatric)."

The policy's Definitions section further states, describing the clinical picture relevant to decompression surgery:

"Radicular Pain: Pain which radiates from the spine into the extremity along the course of the spinal nerve root... Presenting symptoms should include a positive nerve root tension sign (positive straight leg raise test or femoral tension sign), or a reflex, sensory, or motor deficit that correspond to the specific affected nerve root... As surgery is meant to relieve Radicular Pain from nerve root compression, imaging should show compression of the corresponding nerve root."

I have not been able to independently obtain the full text of the InterQual® "Decompression +/- Fusion, Lumbar" module referenced in the policy, because it is a licensed clinical criteria set that is not published for member or public access. I am not quoting that module and am not attributing any specific pass/fail thresholds to it beyond what is stated above, because I have not seen its text. I respectfully request, as part of this appeal, that the plan identify the specific criterion or criteria within that InterQual module that my case was found not to satisfy, so that I may respond to it directly, and that the plan provide a copy of that criteria document to me and to Dr. Lindqvist free of charge, consistent with the plan's claims-and-appeals disclosure obligations.

**2. Clinical record supporting medical necessity**

Applying the record from my prior authorization packet to the elements the policy itself identifies as relevant to lumbar decompression (imaged nerve root compression, correlating radicular symptoms, positive provocative testing, and a corresponding neurologic deficit), the following facts apply:

- Symptom duration and course: I have had 9 months of progressive lower back pain, unrelieved by rest.
- Imaging: MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-06-17 demonstrates an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root — imaging-confirmed compression of the nerve root corresponding to my symptoms, consistent with the policy's own statement that "imaging should show compression of the corresponding nerve root."
- Radicular symptoms and exam findings: I have radicular pain radiating into the right calf, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level — findings consistent with the policy's definition of "Radicular Pain," which calls for "a positive nerve root tension sign ... or a reflex, sensory, or motor deficit that correspond[s] to the specific affected nerve root."
- Functional limitation: I am unable to stand for more than 10 minutes due to pain.
- Documented conservative (non-surgical) treatment prior to seeking surgery:
  - Supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility training, over 10 weeks (2026-04-17 to 2026-06-26), with 16 visits completed, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
  - NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief.
  - Corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-02, which produced only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- Absence of contraindications: I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker.

**3. Requested action**

Given the above, I ask that the plan:
1. Reverse the denial and authorize CPT 63030 as medically necessary; or
2. If the plan maintains that specific InterQual criteria are unmet, identify exactly which criteria and what additional documentation, if any, would resolve the gap, so that Dr. Lindqvist's office can supply it promptly; and
3. Confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and provide the applicable appeal timeframe for a decision.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-16, and I am submitting it well within that deadline. Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the contact information above, and please also copy Dr. Lindqvist's office at [surgeon's office fax/phone/address] as my authorized representative for clinical matters related to this request.

Enclosed with this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-17 to 2026-06-26, 16 visits)
- Records of NSAID trial and corticosteroid injection dated 2026-04-02
- MRI lumbar spine report dated 2026-06-17
- Office/exam notes documenting provocative testing and neurologic deficit
- [Any letter of medical necessity from Dr. Lindqvist, if available]
- [Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination, POC-E6EF62D505-92473]

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Jordan Iverson
